> (S) It was waiting, but it carries the lead it was billed for destroying H (R10 bills the caller), so its wake lands 3-4 slices late. That's the scheduler as designed.

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `aafcbb4144445b9e8b0d9fe754727b15` · 2026-10-01T14:38:04Z

> Do the latency targets count the checked build's audits?
> 
> 1. GATE1 missed the 40 ms deadline-notice target on rv64 (p99 66.9 ms). The cause is confirmed, and it is not the shipped kernel. Right after each destruction, in the same uninterruptible kernel entry, a checked build runs full audit scans: the process and IRQ indexes over every object frame, every RAM frame's owner, and every slot of every live handle table. A process-object free runs one more. With two full handle tables live these take about 24 ms and 8 ms. Production kernels compile none of it. With the two audit calls removed locally, the gate passes: notice 21.6/23.2 ms, R10 23.6 ms, lease end 32 ms, budget_destroy 31 ms (was 110). Every latency target is measured in a checked build, because the scheduler trace only compiles there (R23). Should the targets count audit time? Full write-up: .wash/local/GATE1-notice-late-architect.md, section 7.
>    - (A) Exclude audits (recommended) (recommended): K15 (kernel, Tier A, size S, needs K12): the traced kernel stamps each audit's start and end as test-only records. The oracle and post-check subtract audit time inside each window (deadline notice, wakes, lease end) and report the total. scheduling.md#responsiveness and testbench.md ('Checked builds') state that targets exclude the audits. The audits stay full, no target moves, the attacker is unchanged, and GATE1 runs as is.
>    - (B) Scope or defer audits: Keep the measure gross, and shrink the audits to fit: check only what each destruction touched, or run the full scans only at quiet points such as a case's end. Cheaper, but it weakens the checked build's audit exactly where the gate attacks. The focused fault cases would keep full audits.
>    - (C) Make audits fast enough: Keep the measure gross and the audits full, and rewrite the scans (handle chains, frame owners) until they fit inside 40 ms with two full tables live. A rewrite of debug-only kernel code, and unlikely to fit.
>    - (D) Measure without debug assertions: Run the latency targets on a build without debug assertions. The trace would then have to compile without them, which ends R23's guarantee that a release kernel carries no test channel. A tenet-level change; I recommend against it.
